sense.text:
Revelation 4 is a vision of the kingdom. Some of what John witnesses in heaven is beyond what we can explain here. This is John the Apostle, the disciple who was always on Christ's bosom, one of the chief three apostles, not John the Baptist. He was banished to Patmos and recorded this around AD 96, years after Jerusalem's destruction.

The door opens in heaven and the voice sounds like a trumpet, calling him up to see what must be hereafter. John was not the only apostle given revelations. Paul also saw visions, although the Corinthians disrespected him as a little man with a big mouth. Paul was not behind the chiefest apostles in what the Lord had shown him.

John is immediately in the spirit and sees a throne set in heaven with one sitting on it. The one on the throne is the Father, the Most High. Daniel also saw him as the Ancient of days. He has a body, a garment and hair; he is not a puff of smoke floating in the atmosphere.

He appears like jasper and a sardine stone, sardius. Those stones have a similar colour; the emerald is greenish. Looking at the stones helps us understand what John describes, just as the beryl stone helps with the description of Christ's body elsewhere.

There is a rainbow around the throne, in sight like an emerald. People say there is no colour in the kingdom of heaven, but a rainbow has colour. This rainbow is not the LGBT community. It was already in heaven before God established it in the earth as the sign of his covenant. Many things in heaven are established on earth at different times.

precepts.why:
Paul was going through the regions of Achaia teaching the gospel, and no man was going to stop that boasting. The Corinthians were disrespecting him, so he had to remind them that he was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles.

“For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we have not preached”. Another Jesus comes with another spirit and another gospel. Since the Renaissance our people have been taught a different Jesus. They say his appearance does not matter, only his message, as though the white man lied about Christ's image but told the truth about the gospel. No: the false Christ has a false spirit and a false gospel attached to it.

That is what the famous Christian preachers and gospel singers fail to understand. T. D. Jakes, Creflo, Bynum, the Winans, Yolanda Adams, Fred Hammond, Kirk Franklin, Bobby Jones and Donnie McClurkin remain in that teaching. Bearing with them means rebuking them sharply with the scriptures. Paul is not inferior to the apostles they favour; he also received visions from the Lord.

Paul says it is not expedient to glory in himself, then comes to visions and revelations of the Lord. The man in Christ above fourteen years ago is Paul himself, speaking of the spiritual man without boasting in his flesh. He cannot tell whether he was in the body or out of it; God knows.

He was caught up to the third heaven. The first heaven is our sky and atmosphere, the second is the space we see at night, and the third is where the Most High and the angels dwell. Paul had been stoned to death and revived through the apostles' prayers, then insisted on going back into the city to teach. That is why he speaks of not knowing whether he was in or out of the body.

He was caught into paradise and heard unspeakable words, “which it is not lawful for a man to utter.” The Lord did not allow him to write down what he was shown. He will glory in that man who was caught up, but of himself only in his infirmities. John's written revelations do not mean Paul had never seen those heavenly things.

Daniel beheld the thrones cast down: the kingdoms of the earth destroyed. The Ancient of days sat. He is called Ancient of days because he existed before days, before the light and before the evening and morning of the first day.

His garment is white as snow. A garment requires a body; God is not a puff of smoke. “and the hair of his head like the pure wool”. That woolly hair proves God is a black man, not a man with thin, straight hair. His throne is like a fiery flame, an inferno, and his wheels burn with fire. Those wheels are the chariots described in Ezekiel. This is the Father sitting on the throne John sees.

God sets his bow in the cloud as the token of a covenant between himself and the earth. When clouds gather, the bow appears and he remembers his covenant with every living creature: the waters will not again become a flood destroying all flesh.

The rainbow already existed around the heavenly throne. God established that heavenly thing upon the earth as an everlasting covenant. The same pattern will appear with other things John sees: what God set before him in heaven was also shown and established below.

sense.text: The twenty-four elders sit around the throne clothed in white raiment with crowns of gold. They are elders over every hour of the day, twenty-four hours. The fuller explanation of those elders belongs to another lesson.

Lightnings, thunderings and voices proceed from the throne. Seven lamps of fire burn before it, the seven Spirits of God. This is the seven-branched menorah in heaven. The angels are burning lamps of fire before the Lord in that shape.

The menorah Moses established on earth came from the heavenly pattern. It was not a little ornament sitting on a table. It stood large, made of pure gold, and was to remain lit continually. The Roman relief and the painting of Jerusalem's fall show several men carrying it away. Rome stole it in AD 70. The kingdom coming and God's will being done in earth as in heaven has levels: the rainbow and the menorah are examples of heavenly things established here.

precepts.why:
The candlestick is the menorah, made of pure gold and beaten work, with its shaft, branches, bowls, knops and flowers of the same material. The gold was beautifully decorated. Six branches came out of the central shaft, three on either side. That makes seven with the centre, not eight as Amalek has it.

“And look that thou make them after their pattern, which was shewed thee in the mount.” Moses was shown the pattern, not merely told about it. God gave him a glimpse of the heavenly menorah and told him to make it like that. Its earthly design came from what was already in heaven.

“Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things”. Moses was admonished when he was about to make the tabernacle to make all things according to the pattern shown in the mount. The tabernacle came before the temple. Its furnishings were the example and shadow of things in heaven, explaining why John's vision contains what God commanded Moses to make on earth.

sense.text: John writes to the seven churches in Asia, meaning Asia Minor above the Mediterranean Sea, not China. Grace and peace come from the one who is, was and is to come, and from the seven Spirits before his throne. Those seven Spirits correspond to the menorah: angels before the throne, burning like its lamps.

precepts.why: “Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire:”. God's angels are spirits and his ministers are flaming fire. The seven burning lamps John sees are seven angels before the Lord, in the shape of the menorah. The description is showing the living heavenly reality behind the earthly candlestick.

sense.text: The seven lamps burn before the throne and are the seven Spirits of God, seven angels burning with fire. Even a glimpse of that heavenly sight is beyond what our minds are used to. The prophets describe being overwhelmed when they see such things.

The sea of glass like crystal corresponds to the water in the laver and the molten sea established for the service of God. The water surrounding that great vessel gives the earthly example of what is before the heavenly throne.

The four beasts in the midst of and around the throne are four archangels, male angels, cherubs. They are full of eyes before and behind. Imagine actually seeing those eyes everywhere; it would be a terrifying sight, not the little picture people ordinarily have of an angel.

One beast is like a lion, another a calf, another has a man's face and another is like a flying eagle. Ezekiel saw the same four beasts and described their four faces together. John describes the face dominating the front of each one: lion, ox, man or eagle. The differing descriptions concern how those faces are presented, not different kinds of creatures.

Each has six wings, full of eyes within. The illustration shows the eyes, the hands beneath, the calf-like feet and the wheel within a wheel, helping us picture how strange the sight is. They do not rest day or night but continually proclaim God's holiness, the Almighty who was, is and is to come. These are not the only creatures God has made that we have never seen; even the depths of the sea contain unfamiliar creatures.

precepts.why:
A laver of brass, with a brass foot, is set between the tabernacle of the congregation and the altar and filled with water. Aaron and his sons wash their hands and feet before entering or approaching the altar to minister. “they shall wash with water, that they die not”. Washing for this service is a statute through their generations.

The pictured vessel has water filling the upper part and coming from the mouths of the brass oxen, filling the area where the Levites washed. Its size is apparent beside the men. This water and washing help explain the sea like crystal before the throne.

The Pharisees took the washing required for service in the tabernacle and temple and applied it as a law in the street. That is the issue with the handwashing dispute mentioned in Matthew 15. It is not permission to walk around eating with dirty hands; the point is that the temple requirement was being imposed outside its appointed setting.

The molten sea is round, ten cubits across, five cubits high, about ten feet, with a line of thirty cubits around it. Knops encircle it in two cast rows. It stands on twelve oxen, three facing each direction, north, west, south and east, with their hinder parts inward.

The vessel rests above the oxen. It is a hand breadth thick, with a brim like a cup worked with flowers of lilies, and holds two thousand baths. Water fills it and comes from the mouths of the oxen in the pictured arrangement. The name sea and all that water explain the sea of glass like crystal in John's vision.

All four have the face of a man, a lion on the right, an ox on the left and an eagle. Their wings stretch upward, two joined to one another and two covering their bodies. Ezekiel is describing the same beasts John sees.

Ezekiel gives the four faces together; John's lion, calf, man and eagle identify the face that dominates the front of each creature. Their appearance, eyes and wings are far beyond anything we normally encounter. Seeing such a creature would make a person fear, lose bodily control and feel his spirit leave him. Do not assume God's creation is limited to the familiar animals around us.

sense.text: The Egyptians were deceived into worshipping serpents void of reason and vile beasts. God sent unreasonable beasts against them for vengeance, so that they would know a man can be punished by the very thing with which he sins. The creatures they honoured became part of their punishment.

The Almighty hand made the world from matter without form. God did not lack the power to send multitudes of bears or fierce lions. His choice of creatures for a judgment is not limited by his ability.

“Or unknown wild beasts, full of rage, newly created”. Esau thinks he has seen everything, but Solomon, the wisest man, speaks of unknown creatures. They are full of rage; you cannot pacify them or tell them to roll over and play dead. They breathe fiery vapour or filthy scents of scattered smoke and shoot horrible sparkles from their eyes. The ideas behind creatures such as Godzilla did not come from nowhere; men have been reading these scriptures.

Their harm can destroy people, and even the terrible sight can do so. That is why seeing the heavenly beasts could make a person's spirit leave him. God has strange creations in heaven and earth we have not beheld. Think of the angler fish deep in the sea, with great teeth and a light on an antenna: that is only a glimpse of what is below, not proof that we have found it all.

On the fifth day God commanded the seventh part, where the waters were gathered, to bring forth living creatures, fowls and fishes. Man was created on the sixth day. The seventh part here means the waters, the oceans. The birds came from the sea, formed from the dust at its bottom and brought through the water. Water without life brought forth living things at God's command so that people might praise his works.

Two creatures were ordained, Enoch and Leviathan. Enoch is another name for Behemoth. God separated them because the waters could not hold both together. These mighty beasts were not to live in the same place.

Enoch, Behemoth, received the part dried up on the third day, the land with a thousand hills. The dry earth was made on the third day. Behemoth is the land creature, not an ordinary elephant. Job describes its strength, bones and huge tail.

These are species, not just one Behemoth and one Leviathan. The strange bones men find tell them of creatures unlike the ordinary animals they see. Jurassic Park and Journey to the Center of the Earth express the search for such creatures and hidden places where they might still be. We have not seen everything on earth, much less everything in heaven.

Leviathan received the seventh part, the moist, meaning the oceans. The Lord keeps that creature for destruction at the time and against the people he chooses. Ships disappearing in the Bermuda Triangle, with neither ship nor crew left to find, are an example of being swallowed up. The enormous water creature in Jurassic World that seizes the other dinosaur and drags it under gives an illustration of Leviathan's size and power.

precepts.why:
Behemoth is the Enoch named in Esdras. Some Bibles suggest an elephant, but read the description. It eats grass like an ox, not meat. Its strength is in its loins and belly, and it moves its tail like a cedar, a great tree. An elephant's little tail is not like a cedar; this tail is so huge that a blow from it would kill a man.

Its sinews are bound together, its bones like strong brass and bars of iron. It is the chief of God's ways. Only the one who made it can bring his sword near it; no man can simply overpower this creature. That is why God separated Behemoth from Leviathan.

The mountains bring it food, matching Esdras's thousand hills, and the other beasts play there. It lies under shady trees among reeds and fens, with willows around it. It can drink up a river without hurrying and trusts that it can draw Jordan into its mouth. Other animals scatter when a lion comes to drink; Behemoth is not running from anything before it has finished. No snare man makes will capture it. That is not the description of an ordinary elephant.

sense.text: The beasts give glory, honour and thanks to the one on the throne, who lives for ever. Think of their continual singing. Judah can sing, though that spirit was on Levi in the scriptures, but these creatures are beyond even our best singers. Imagine multiple vocal cords in one beast, able to sound every note and octaves we have never heard, in perfect harmony. God does not have bad singers praising him. Do not compare that heavenly ability to somebody merely believing she can sing along with Whitney Houston.
The twenty-four elders fall down, worship the one who lives for ever and cast their crowns before the throne. Their authority does not remove the need to give him honour and thanks.

The Lord is worthy of glory, honour and power because he created all things for his pleasure. The next part of the vision concerns the scroll sealed with seven seals. A seal belongs to one in authority; a sealed writing cannot simply be opened by anyone. No man in heaven, earth or the grave could open that scroll. Christ alone is worthy to break its seals and reveal it.

The first seal reveals conquest of nations under the guise of righteousness. The second identifies the red, warlike race that conquers and makes war worldwide with the great sword. The third reveals that same race controlling the world's economy. The fourth shows death, hell, pestilence and disease following its conquests.

The fifth reveals the souls of righteous Israelites asking vengeance against that same race for what it has done. The sixth ushers in World War III, with the kings of the earth hiding at the Lord's return. The seventh brings the destruction of Babylon the great, the United States of America. These are the things Christ makes known by opening the seals. The fourth seal's pestilence also raises the question of why people are so afraid of the coronavirus.

The secret place of the Most High is the Bible. Dwelling there means abiding under the Almighty's shadow, his protection, where the heat cannot burn you. The Lord is our refuge and fortress; put your trust in him.

The sisters panicking on Facebook over the coronavirus need to examine that trust. AIDS, Ebola, Zika, SARS, swine flu, bird flu and mad cow disease have already come and gone as the thing everybody fears. The sisters slandering, gossiping and carrying evil spirits are nervous because they know they are not right. Stay in God's secret place instead of spreading panic or running after every warning.

Do not shave your beard because somebody claims it will give you coronavirus or stop you getting a job. People without beards are catching it. Do not let that claim make you forsake the commandments. The fear about going to Chinese nail and hair shops is another reason to stop depending on those people.

A fowler catches birds with traps. God delivers his people from the snares Esau lays and from the noisome pestilence, meaning disease. He covers them with his feathers, and they trust under his wings. His truth is his law, their shield and buckler. A shield is the larger protection against a sword and a buckler the smaller shield. The law is the protection to rely on, not panic buying every bottle of Lysol because the label mentions coronavirus.

Do not fear the terror by night, the arrow by day or the pestilence walking in darkness. The arrow is nuclear weapons and the pestilence includes coronavirus, Ebola and Zika. Do not go around terrified, assuming a baby's cold is coronavirus or coming to school wearing a mask out of fear. Pray to the Lord and keep faith.

“nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” There is a mystery in that timing: the destruction happens at noon. The fourth seal reveals the conquering race bringing death, hell, pestilence and disease, but God's people are to dwell in his protection.

precepts.why: “Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.”. The Lord reveals his secret to his servants the prophets. Those secrets are in the scriptures, explaining why dwelling in the secret place means dwelling in the Bible rather than living in fear of every new disease.

The secret things belong to the Lord, but the revealed things belong to us and our children for ever, so that we may do all the words of this law. The secrets are bound to the law in the Bible. God's protection is connected to receiving and doing what he has revealed, not ignoring it while panicking over the world.

sense.text: The angels gave thanks to the one on the throne; Paul likewise teaches the brothers and sisters in Colosse to give thanks to the Father. He has made us fit to share the inheritance of the saints in light. Giving him thanks is the response to what he has prepared for us.

The power of darkness is Satan's kingdom, Babylon, Rome, the realm in which the white man rules. Darkness is sin. The Father delivers us from that power and translates us into the kingdom of his dear Son. Leaving that darkness means learning and following the light Christ brought.

Redemption and forgiveness come through Christ's blood. Without his sacrifice we can do nothing. Evil is present even when we want to do good; that nature is in every man and woman from the womb. Watch a child take candy when nobody is looking, or strike another child who receives the toy he wanted. The evil nature does not have to be taught, but the light, God's laws, must be taught.

Christ is the image of the invisible God and the firstborn of every creature. Firstborn means exactly that: he is the first of the Father's creations. That is why he is the only begotten Son. He is not merely another prophet. Proverbs explains his existence with the Father before the earth and the rest of creation.

precepts.why: The fifth angel pours his vial on the seat of the beast, and its kingdom is full of darkness while they gnaw their tongues for pain. The beast is the so-called white man. The place where he rules is the kingdom of darkness, Satan's realm, from which the Father delivers his people. The darkness translates to sin.

Light came into the world, but men loved darkness rather than light because their deeds were evil. Christ is that light: the Messiah, lawkeeper, lawgiver and teacher who magnified God's law. People prefer the darkness because sin is pleasurable. Deliverance from the kingdom of darkness requires turning away from that preference.

“Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. Sin's pleasure is temporary. A brother or sister arranges a meeting through Facebook, enjoys fifteen or thirty minutes, then finds out they contracted a disease. Was that pleasure worth it? They ask why God did it while forgetting their own choice.

The drug dealer makes quick money but is always looking over his shoulder, worried about the police or another dealer who wants to take him out. That is no way to live. The pleasure lasts only a season and brings consequences; choose affliction with God's people over that darkness.

sense.text: The me in this passage is Christ. The chapter speaks of wisdom, and Christ is the wisdom of God. The Father possessed him in the beginning of his way, before the old works. Christ was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed. That is what firstborn of every creature means.

Before the depths of seas and oceans or fountains abounding with water, Christ was brought forth. He existed before the mountains, hills, earth, fields or highest dust of the world. He was the Father's first creation, before Michael, Uriel and the other angels, not somebody whose existence began only when he appeared among men.

When the Father prepared the heavens, Christ was there. The compass on the face of the depth is a circle, north, south, east and west. He was present when the clouds were established, the fountains strengthened, the sea given its boundary and the earth its foundations. Every stage of creation came after him.

“Then I was by him, as one brought up with him”. Christ was daily the Father's delight, rejoicing before him, in the habitable earth and with the sons of men. He was there when man was made in their image. The Father has favourites, and Christ was first. This explains John's testimony that Christ was before him and the Word was with God in the beginning.

precepts.why: “He that cometh after me is preferred before me: for he was before me.” John the Baptist is speaking more deeply than the order in which they appeared on earth. Christ was the first of the Father's creations and his delight, as Proverbs 8 explains. His preference and existence precede John.

sense.text: The Word was in the beginning, was with God and was God. This is Christ with the Father, the same relationship explained in Proverbs 8. He was there before the rest of creation, brought up with the Father and daily his delight.

All things were made by him, and without him nothing made was made. He was brought forth before the heavens, earth, mountains, hills, seas and depths, and those things were made through him. Firstborn of every creature and only begotten Son are not empty titles.

The same Word who was with the Father became flesh and dwelt among us. His glory is the glory of the only begotten of the Father because he is first of all the creations. When Christ calls himself Alpha and Omega, the first and last, beginning and end, he means it. Let the explanation in Proverbs sink into your spirit.

precepts.why: “Then I was by him, as one brought up with him”. That is the meaning of the Word being with God. Christ was with the Father before everything else was made, not merely a prophet introduced after the world already existed.

sense.text: All things in heaven and earth, visible and invisible, thrones, dominions, principalities and powers, were created by Christ and for him. He is before all things and by him they consist. Proverbs 8 and John's opening already explained it. Christ is much more than a regular prophet.

Christ is the head of the body, the church, the beginning and the firstborn from the dead. He has the preeminence in all things, both as the first creation and the firstborn from the dead. The Father was pleased that all fullness should dwell in him.

The church is not the Roman Catholic Church. Church means the general assembly, Israel, the people who were with Moses in the wilderness and received the lively oracles. Christ is the head of that assembly.

Peace is made through the blood of Christ's cross to reconcile all things to himself. Do not run past the word reconcile. It means restore to friendship or harmony: a relationship existed, was lost, and is brought back. It does not mean starting an entirely new relationship with people who never had one.

The reconciliation is of the children of Israel. Under Ezekiel's order, sacrifices reconciled the house of Israel; now Christ's sacrifice does it. If someone claims this means every race, ask when the Jebusites, Philistines, Moabites or Ammonites were in that friendship with the Lord. There is no chapter establishing that former covenant with them. The prior relationship belongs to Israel.

Paul was made a minister by God's dispensation to fulfill the word and reveal the mystery hidden through ages and generations. It is now manifested to the saints, the Israelites. The Gentiles here are the northern kingdom, who must also know the riches of this mystery: Christ in you, the hope of glory.

Christ is the Father's first creation, promised from Genesis, the king of kings and Lord of lords coming through Israel. He is not every race and colour, a Rainbow Coalition; he is of Judah and comes for the nation of Israel. We will rule under him as joint-heirs. The world rejects that mystery. Faith in Christ is necessary to receive the spiritual understanding of the scriptures.

precepts.why: The general assembly is the church of the firstborn, written in heaven, with God the judge of all and the spirits of just men made perfect. Christ is the firstborn and head of that church. General assembly explains the word church; it does not identify the Roman Catholic institution as Christ's body.

Moses told the children of Israel that God would raise a prophet from their brethren, whom they must hear. That prophet is Christ, though he is more than a regular prophet. Moses was in the church in the wilderness with the angel speaking on Sinai and the fathers who received the lively oracles to give to us.

The church in the wilderness was the Israelites. The lively oracles are the law given to them. That identifies the general assembly over which Christ is head and rules out the claim that the church here is the Roman Catholic Church.

The command to the married is that the wife not depart from her husband; if she departs, she remains unmarried or is reconciled to him. Reconciled means restored to the friendship or harmony they had before the separation. It is not a new marriage to a stranger.

That ordinary example makes the meaning clear when Paul uses reconcile in Colossians. A previous relationship has to exist before it can be restored. Do not let someone pass over that word and turn Israel's reconciliation into a claim about every race.

The prince here is the priest. His part is to provide the burnt, meat and drink offerings in the feasts, new moons, sabbaths and solemnities of the house of Israel. The sin, meat, burnt and peace offerings make reconciliation for the house of Israel.

Those animal sacrifices restored Israel's relationship with the Father. Paul is now speaking of the sacrifice of Christ and the blood of his cross. The sacrifice changes, but the people being reconciled are still the children of Israel.

sense.text:
“Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures”. Only Christ opens spiritual understanding. People rejecting Christ can read the Bible as a novel or read Christian commentaries, but that is not the understanding given by the Son of God.

The Old Testament-only group calling themselves Israelites, the Yayas, do not have that spirit. This is not aimed at a brother merely named Yisrael. Rejecting Christ leaves them arguing on Facebook rather than going face to face on the streets and answering through the scriptures. Accept the Son as Messiah, King of kings and Lord of lords if you want that understanding.

Two disciples went toward Emmaus, about sixty furlongs from Jerusalem, discussing what had happened. Christ drew near and walked with them, but their eyes were held so they did not recognize him. He asked why they were sad and what they were discussing.

One was Cleopas. These were other disciples, not Peter, James or John. They described Jesus of Nazareth, mighty in deed and word before God and the people, delivered by the chief priests and rulers to be condemned and crucified. They were speaking to Christ without recognizing him.

Their eyes opened, they knew him, and he vanished from their sight. Picture that: after explaining the scriptures, he was recognized and then gone. They remembered their hearts burning while he talked with them and opened the scriptures. Opening means breaking them down so the disciples understood.

We need that burning zeal when hearing God's word. Remember first finding out you were Israel and wanting to learn everything in one day. You did not care about the football game or boxing; you wanted the scriptures. If you have lost that spirit, pray for it to return. New people may not be there yet, but those who once had that fire should seek it again.

precepts.why:
Jeremiah became sick of the Israelites and said he would not speak any more in the Lord's name. “But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones”. He grew weary of holding it back and could not stay silent.

That is the same burning Cleopas described. You can go to the street saying you will let the brothers teach, then hear somebody's foolishness and feel the scriptures burning until you ask for the microphone. The word moves you to speak even when you planned to hold back.

The Comforter, the Holy Ghost sent by the Father in Christ's name, teaches all things and brings them to remembrance. Test a Christian's claim to have that Holy Ghost. After twenty, forty-six or sixty years, has it revealed that Christmas is a lie, that they are Israelites, or that they should not eat shrimp, crab, pork and swine?

If none of those things has been brought to remembrance, the claim does not match Christ's promise. You do not have the Holy Ghost; you have an unholy demon. The Comforter's teaching is shown by the understanding and remembrance of God's word, not merely announcing that you possess it.

sense.text:
The Father created all things, beginning with Christ, for his pleasure. We are in the greatest movie of all time, for lack of a better word. A movie needs a script, actors and actresses, good characters and bad characters. The Bible is the greatest story, and Israel is its main people.

Some of the heroes fall. When people fall out or are put to death, that also has its place in what God wrote. Everything does not go the way we expect, but the whole creation serves his pleasure. Our own experiences, including the painful ones, become examples from which others must learn.

The Lord commands the wife not to depart from her husband. A godly man was supposed to marry a godly woman. Ordinary problems in a marriage, financial difficulties or occasional sexual problems, are different from physical violence. The command does not mean a woman must remain in danger with a violent man.

Some sisters married a wicked man whose quick tongue, good looks or fighting first attracted them. The clever mouth is now turned on her, and the rough neck she admired now kicks and hits her. Some men also have violent wives, but the immediate counsel here is to the sisters.

“But and if she depart, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband”. If you are married to a violent man, separate from him. We are not proponents of divorce, but we advise separation when there is violence. Notice the or: remaining unmarried and reconciliation are distinct possibilities, not a command to hurry back.

Reconcile means restore friendly relations and harmony. It comes after counseling and after going out with him under a chaperone so there is evidence that his spirit is in check. This takes months, plural, not a week or one month. Anger may be about his job, another woman he wanted or other frustrations, but none of that excuses hitting his wife. If he complains she has let herself go, take her to the gym; do not beat her.

When courting, ask the right questions and learn the family background. If possible, meet the parents. A home where parents curse, kick and hit each other can pass those characteristics to their children. Two years in the truth does not automatically erase a lifetime of abuse. Watch his friends and how he treats them: if he belittles and calls them names, expect that behaviour to appear toward you as well.

Sister Bina came to the Atlanta leadership three times about her husband's violence, and he was removed three times. She was told to stay away because he was not ready. She eventually felt the leadership was keeping her from her man and left to be with him. The report of her death shows why this counsel is given and why reconciliation cannot simply be assumed.

precepts.why:
A naughty person, a wicked man, walks with a froward mouth. Froward means he speaks evil. A woman may first find that witty, fast-talking man attractive, then discover that the same mouth is turned against her.

He winks with his eyes, speaks with his feet and teaches with his fingers. The wink is how he approached her on the subway, bus or street. The feet and fingers describe his violence: she may have admired him beating another man, wanting a rough neck or soldier, but now the kicks and slaps are directed at her. Recognize that wickedness rather than treating it as a sign of love.

“The Lord shall smite thee with madness”. Madness includes being psychologically imbalanced. Our people, black and brown, including Puerto Ricans, are coming out of dysfunctional and violent households. Joy DeGruy's explanation of post-traumatic slave disorder addresses the trauma for which our people have never received counseling.

Do not assume that entering the truth instantly removed that history. Learn how the person grew up, meet the family and observe the circle of friends. Abuse learned through a lifetime takes time to overcome. These questions are necessary before marriage and before assuming a violent spouse is ready to reconcile.

sense.text:
“Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls”. The leadership's counsel is intended to protect you. Some grew up without a father; now there are men looking out for them, but they reject those men when the counsel interferes with the relationship they want. If we tell you to stay away from a violent man, listen.

Sister Bina was a quiet, good sister with children. Her husband was removed three times for beating her, and she was told to leave him alone. She left IUIC about a year ago so she could be with him. He killed her this week, shooting her in front of her son. The corrected account is that he stabbed his first girlfriend and shot Sister Bina. Pray for her children and family in this difficult time.

There is one rule across IUIC: if a man hits his wife and it can be proved, he must go. He does not remain among the congregation doing that evil. He has to get himself right, and he may be gone a long time. A real man does not need to put his hands on his wife. Being emotional, raised by his mother or angry at something in life does not excuse violence. The man who fears hitting another brother but beats his wife is not showing strength. You are a black ashy devil, not a righteous Israelite merely because you claim the name.

Sisters, do not cover for these men. Report the violence to the police, get a police report and have the man locked up. Do not bail him out. Leaving him there makes him face what he did. The leadership is not the police. In the past, men retaliated against an abusive husband, then the sister threatened to report the leadership's retaliation when she did not get what she wanted. We are not doing that again. Report the offense through the police instead of expecting the congregation to beat him for you.

The Bible is the hedge of protection described in Psalms 91. Rejecting its counsel removes that protection. The lesson from what happened is to get yourself right and heed the warning while there is time. Some women think a man does not love them unless he hits them. No: he hits because he hates your guts. Violence can become so normal in a broken family that a woman smacks her boyfriend on a train and laughs while everyone around them is alarmed. That is not a healthy expression of love.

The warning applies to men as well. If leadership says a sister is not ready or tells you to stay away, there may be private information that cannot be disclosed. We cannot expose everybody's confidential business and still expect people to trust us in counseling. Ask the right questions, not merely a large number of questions. Brothers should not get angry at that instruction; it may concern a violent history, a disease or something else that can harm them.

A New York brother ignored the warning about a sister who had come from a shelter, secretly slept with her and then faced accusations, including an accusation concerning her daughter, which he denied. Another brother preparing to betroth a woman found her arguing with a wall and left. Another couple was violent on both sides: he shut her in a closet and blocked it with a sofa, and she later cut his asthma equipment while laughing as he struggled to breathe. A spare device hidden in his cabinet saved him. These are the kinds of situations the counsel is trying to prevent.

A backdoor marriage does not become safe merely because the couple stays together for two or three years or starts working its way back. The danger can appear later. Ask which brothers or sisters the person counsels with. A brother in Riverdale was asked whom his intended wife spoke with and whether she attended the Titus 2 classes. He did not know, then learned she did not attend. He took the advice to wait. Some brothers and sisters do take counsel, and that is good; this correction is not aimed at every sister.

Another man married against advice and woke to voodoo objects in his house: a coconut under the bed, salt in the corner and paper in his shoes to bind him to her. Another was impressed by a woman who could quote five scriptures against every one he gave, thinking her knowledge made her ready. He showed his own blood test but told her she did not need one because she was God-fearing. Months later she confessed she had herpes and claimed God wanted him to have it. Scripture knowledge and religious language do not replace asking the necessary questions and checking the actual conduct.

There are rules in IUIC as there are rules at a workplace. Laughter and jokes do not mean the rules are a game; lives are involved. One sister came to the school with a .38-calibre gun threatening suicide after her man left her. Deacon Asaph got the gun from her and the sisters counseled her. Years later a brother insisted on marrying her. When warned that she was suicidal, he repeated the confidential warning to her. That is why intimate counseling details are not freely disclosed to prospective spouses.

He married her anyway, spent money fixing his teeth to satisfy her and later bought the Audi she wanted. He left aviation school and worked two jobs to meet her demands. She controlled him by threatening to kill herself if he did not do what she said. When he lost a job, he was afraid to tell her. He became smaller and worn down, and she pulled him out of the truth. Learn from what happened instead of demanding confidential details or assuming desire makes someone ready.

Look at the person's circle. If somebody has been among us four years but only surrounds himself or herself with brand-new people, ask why. Newcomers are easier to manipulate. If a man has been a soldier for nine years without promotion, ask the right questions about his conduct. Do not let an attractive appearance keep you from examining those things.

These stories are told without naming the people in order to warn new brothers and sisters, not to humiliate them. The experiences become a testimony of what not to do. Sister Bina said she left because there was no food in the house, but the Riverdale pantry had free food, with deliveries every Thursday and brothers and sisters working to provide it. The underlying issue was wanting to return to the man the leadership would not allow to keep beating her. Do not conceal violence or use another reason to evade the warning. A brother doing this must leave and get himself right.

“If any brother hath a wife that believeth not, and she be pleased to dwell with him”. Pleased to dwell means the unbelieving husband or wife is doing what the Bible says, including coming here, though that person does not yet believe. It does not mean a sister can call her husband pleased to dwell when she does not know where he is, he does not know where she is, and after two or three years nobody has ever seen him.

Some boast about an unbelieving husband on social media because he provides a comfortable life. Another asked whether to stay with a husband who went to strip clubs every Thursday and wanted sex with her afterward. Do not simply accept his assurance that nothing happens in the champagne room. Be careful about the conduct and the danger to the marriage.

The film Temptation: Confessions of a Marriage Counselor illustrates a woman leaving a good, ordinary man for a wealthy, attractive, fast-talking man and contracting AIDS, destroying her marriage. A couples' gathering can watch it with stopping points to discuss the choices. When courting, listen to how the other person responds; that can reveal how they think.

The grass looking greener elsewhere does not mean the other relationship has no problems. There is dirt under that grass too, and it may be dirt you cannot handle. Mow, fertilize and maintain your own lawn. Do not abandon a good marriage for an imagined life on the other side.
